summary: Selected surviving Pro proposal 1 and implemented the opponent-requested exact slack attack. On the unsatisfiable eight-clause formula over three variables, all 64 RS evaluation coordinates can be made zero by one non-Boolean slack bit. The exact finite squared objective is 27 against Boolean baseline 19, giving only sqrt(27/19), not an added residual squared cost of at least 57. This kills the tested residual-only RS gadget, not RS-based reductions in general.
hypothesis: RS spreading amplifies only nonzero affine residuals; free integer clause slacks can instead set every residual to zero while paying a constant unamplified half-integral-anchor penalty.

tests.finding: Exact search certifies squared optimum 27, Boolean baseline 19, zero amplified residual energy, and distance ratio sqrt(27/19); 68,921 variable assignments and 524,288 Boolean variable/slack assignments were checked.

next_experiment: Test a mutation that spreads the Booleanity/slack defects together with clause residuals, with an explicit lattice basis and target; use exact low-weight search to determine whether correlated integer directions can still cancel every amplified block.
